title: Restrict the device signing authority file to owner-only from creation

claims.statement: Claude Code (claude-code) is the source-producing agent for CHG-0068 under human principal @rodrigoteamx, on the 2026-08-24 directive 'dale al merge y a lo que sigue' — the second hardening fix, closing the signing-key file-permission finding. This does not authorize automatic merge of CHG-0068.
claims.evidence: AGENTS.md, profile.json actors and the 2026-08-24 user directive.

claims.statement: The hardening audit found the SQLite authority file — which holds the Ed25519 device-signing private key and every sealed verifier — world-readable during init and permanently if init threw before the final chmod: chmod 0o600 was applied last after several fallible steps, and mkdir's 0o700 mode is silently ignored by Node for a pre-existing directory (the common DATA_DIR case).
claims.evidence: server/src/auth/SqliteDeviceCredentialStore.ts init() prior order; the 2026-08-24 hardening-audit finding hardening-signing-key-file-perms.

claims.statement: The change tightens the directory to 0o700 after mkdir (covering a pre-existing world-readable directory and the transient -journal sidecar created under the process umask) and the file to 0o600 immediately after open — before any secret is written and before any fallible init step — via a win32-guarded restrictPath helper, keeping a final re-assert as belt-and-suspenders.
claims.evidence: server/src/auth/SqliteDeviceCredentialStore.ts restrictPath and the reordered init() chmods.

claims.statement: Governed discovery reordered the fix to tighten permissions before the first secret write rather than after init completes, which closes both the init-window exposure and the permanent throw-before-chmod gap, rather than only narrowing the window.
claims.evidence: The audit finding and the placement of restrictPath immediately after open, before initializeSchema writes the signing key.

claims.statement: Asserting after init that the directory is 0o700 and the file is 0o600 for a pre-existing world-readable directory, and that the file stays 0o600 when init fails after the file is created, proves the exposure is closed.
claims.evidence: server/tests/unit/deviceCredentialStorePermissions.test.ts is the falsification mechanism (POSIX only; skipped on Windows).

claims.statement: The protection is POSIX filesystem permissions only — a no-op on Windows (guarded so it never fails there), no defense against an owner-level process or a host compromise, and the signing key remains plaintext PKCS8 at rest protected by permissions rather than encryption.
claims.evidence: restrictPath swallows chmod errors only on win32; the key is stored as private_key_pkcs8 in SqliteDeviceSigningAuthority.

claims.statement: The change is server-only and additive; no protocol or Studio change and no functional regression.
claims.evidence: git diff of the CHG-0068 branch: server/src/auth/SqliteDeviceCredentialStore.ts and server/tests/unit/deviceCredentialStorePermissions.test.ts.

successCriteria.statement: After init, the authority directory is 0o700 and the file is 0o600, even when the directory pre-existed world-readable.
successCriteria.verification: A POSIX test pre-creates the directory at 0o755, runs init, and asserts the directory is 0o700 and the file 0o600.

successCriteria.statement: The file is owner-only even when init fails after the file is created.
successCriteria.verification: A test injects a beforeCommit failure during schema initialization, asserts init rejects, and asserts the created file is still 0o600.
The full server suite passes and the server type-check passes.

definitionOfDone.statement: CHG-0068 records the signing-key permission finding and its fix before implementation.
definitionOfDone.evidence: Schema-valid record and deterministic governance compilation.

definitionOfDone.statement: init() tightens the directory and file to owner-only before any secret is written, via a win32-guarded helper.
A test proves the directory and file permissions and the failed-init case; the full server suite passes.
Governance, licensing, lint, type-check, focused and full tests, build, dependency audit and diff checks pass before handoff.
definitionOfDone.evidence: npm run governance:check, npm run check, npm run build, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities), ESLint, type-check and git diff --check; the accept commit is verified by its own pull-request Constitution run before merge.
